TokenBatch API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

TokenBatch is the closed ragged result returned by tokenizers, extractors, aligners, and other Note::nlp() or Note::regex() operations whose cells can produce different numbers of strings. A rectangular Note cannot represent those variable-length rows without padding; TokenBatch instead stores one flat Text or Bytes Note plus one Int64 boundary Note.

The Ragged Layout¶

For N logical source cells, offsets() contains N + 1 cumulative boundaries. Source cell r owns the half-open token range

[offsets[r], offsets[r + 1])

inside tokens(). Equal adjacent boundaries encode an empty row. The first boundary is always zero, boundaries never decrease, and the final boundary equals the number of flat tokens. This is a compact, padding-free representation: token text and row structure each occur exactly once.

TokenBatch is a cheap reference-counted handle. Copying it does not copy token bytes or offsets. The tokens() and offsets() accessors return borrowed const Note& references; copy either returned Note handle when it must outlive the particular TokenBatch handle used to obtain it.

State Queries¶

defined() asks whether the handle owns a ragged result. empty() asks whether that result contains zero flat tokens. Those are independent questions: a defined result can be empty because every source cell emitted zero tokens, and a default-constructed undefined handle is also empty.

Every displayed result on these pages is emitted by examples/CodeN/tokenbatch_codec_reference_demo.cpp.
